name: Spatial Partitioning for Parallelism
text:
# Spatial Partitioning for Parallelism


## Overview
Spatial Partitioning for Parallelism divides a volumetric dataset into independent chunks to distribute I/O and computation across multiple processing units, solving the memory and throughput bottlenecks of large-scale volume rendering [G]. It differs from tree-based methods like [Chunk Trees](4050-chunk-trees.md) by using fixed or pre-computed spatial divisions rather than [hierarchical traversal](#896-hierarchical-traversal.md), and from [streaming](#20554-streaming.md) methods like [Chunk-based World Streaming](2369-chunk-based-world-streaming.md) by focusing on static or semi-static data distribution for parallel execution rather than temporal or view-dependent chunk loading [G].

## Shared principles
Builds on [Chunk-based spatial partitioning](3862-chunk-based-spatial-partitioning.md) [G]. The global volume domain $\Omega$ is partitioned into a grid of chunks [G]. For a [regular grid](#3950-regular-grid.md), the chunk index $\mathbf{k} = (k_x, k_y, k_z)$ for a voxel at global coordinate $\mathbf{p} = (x, y, z)$ is calculated as:
$$
k_x = \lfloor x / W_x \rfloor, \quad k_y = \lfloor y / W_y \rfloor, \quad k_z = \lfloor z / W_z \rfloor
$$
where $W_x, W_y, W_z$ are the chunk dimensions in voxels [G]. Each chunk is treated as an independent unit for loading, processing, or rendering [G]. To prevent boundary artifacts (e.g., black stripes in [compositing](#2436-compositing.md) or discontinuities in [isosurfaces](#13788-isosurfaces.md)) caused by naive non-overlapping division, a small overlap of data may be included among adjacent datasets [G]. These extra/duplicated slices are used for boundary calculations but must be removed before final compositing to prevent image stretching [G].

## Subtopics

### [MPI-based Volume Partitioning](1093-mpi-based-volume-partitioning.md)
A data-parallel strategy where a volumetric dataset is partitioned into contiguous chunks of slices, with each [MPI](#21796-multi-plane-images-mpi.md) process reading and rendering only its assigned portion. It partitions the data grid directly rather than clustering geometric primitives, and relies on static process assignment rather than dynamic sharding. Choose it for efficient I/O and [parallel rendering](#9364-parallel-rendering-hybrid-systems.md) of uniform-resolution volumes where contiguous memory access minimizes seek overhead.

### [Object-space decomposition with local clustering](4156-object-space-decomposition-with-local-clustering.md)
A [view-independent preprocessing](#23475-view-independent-preprocessing.md) method for [parallel volume rendering on unstructured grids](#22713-parallel-volume-rendering-for-unstructured-grids.md) that partitions the domain into cell-clusters to minimize communication and load imbalance during rendering. It differs from sibling methods by performing k-way partitioning locally on each processor using MeTiS before global synchronization, and explicitly constructs a contracted visualization graph to support the subsequent [Remapping Phase](4250-remapping-phase.md) for dynamic view adaptation. Choose it for unstructured grids requiring load-balanced, [view-dependent rendering](#17938-view-dependent-data-loading.md) with minimal inter-processor communication.

### [ShardedVolume](12593-shardedvolume.md)
A data structure representing a 3D volume partitioned into multiple shards (sub-arrays) to allow parallel processing or memory management across devices, with methods for arithmetic operations and data access. It solves the problem of managing large volumetric datasets that exceed single-device memory or require distributed computation by treating each shard as an autonomous unit for arithmetic operations and data access. Choose it for managing large volumetric datasets that exceed single-device memory or require distributed computation with high-level API abstractions.

### [One-Phase Remapping Model](16393-one-phase-remapping-model.md)
The [One-Phase Remapping Model](#16393-one-phase-remapping-model.md) is a method for solving the remapping problem in parallel [direct volume rendering](#1184-direct-volume-rendering.md) (DVR) by constructing a single augmented graph (the remapping graph) and performing a single K-way partition, rather than separating partitioning and assignment into two phases. It addresses the limitation of two-phase approaches where decisions made during the initial partitioning phase restrict the quality of the final task-to-processor assignment. By integrating the current mapping and migration costs into the graph structure, it allows a standard graph partitioner to simultaneously optimize load balance and communication/migration overhead. Choose it when two-phase approaches restrict task-to-processor assignment quality and dynamic remapping is required.

### [Graph-Based Distributed Partitioning](19155-graph-based-distributed-partitioning.md)
[Graph-Based Distributed Partitioning](#19155-graph-based-distributed-partitioning.md) is an offline strategy for assigning 3D points (such as 3D Gaussian splats) to distributed GPUs or machines by modeling data access patterns as a bipartite graph and partitioning it to minimize cross-partition communication edges while balancing memory usage. Unlike geometric proximity methods (e.g., KD-trees, k-means) that ignore camera view dependency, this method explicitly accounts for the fact that points far apart in 3D space may be visible to the same camera, thereby reducing the need for inter-GPU communication during rendering. Choose it for large-scale distributed rendering of point-based data where view-dependent locality reduces inter-GPU communication.

### [Slice-Based Data-Space Parallel Distribution](20355-slice-based-data-space-parallel-distribution.md)
[Slice-Based Data-Space Parallel Distribution](#20355-slice-based-data-space-parallel-distribution.md) partitions a 3D voxel dataset into contiguous 2D slices and assigns them to parallel processors to enable [local processing](#5373-independent-block-encoding.md) while minimizing communication overhead. Unlike display-space parallelism, which distributes rendering tasks across the image plane, this method distributes the source data itself, reducing memory requirements per node and leveraging the typically higher resolution in the X-Y plane for efficient loop execution. Choose it for medical imaging workloads where data is naturally recorded on a slice basis and memory per node must be minimized.

### [Direct Send](20759-direct-send.md)
[Direct Send](#20759-direct-send.md) is a parallel volume rendering composition technique for object partitioning where partial images generated by different processors are sent directly to a specific target processor for [final composition](#9992-final-composition.md). It is distinguished from sibling methods like Binary Swap, which relies on iterative pairwise exchanges, and Parallel Pipeline, which arranges processors in a linear sequence. Choose it for straightforward, low-latency composition when a dedicated compositing node is available and network bandwidth can handle bulk transfers.

### Binary Swap
A composition technique for object partitioning on clusters where partial images are exchanged and merged between processors in a binary swap fashion to produce the final image [S1, unofficial]. Transparent pixels can be eliminated in communications using [compression](#4-compression.md) techniques and bounding box structures [S1, unofficial]. It is implemented in the DViz library developed at INRIA Lorraine, which provides a particularly performant implementation [S1, unofficial].
